children: Polish retail sales accelerated in October, exceeding analysts' expectations, driven partly by an increase in fuel sales following the government's reintroduction of a price-cutting package, data showed on Tuesday.

Retail sales at constant prices (PLRSCO=ECI) rose 3.5% in October from a year earlier, accelerating from the 3.3% advance registered in September and exceeding economists' forecasts of 3.1%, the statistics office reported.
At the beginning of October, the government reintroduced a program to limit fuel prices at Polish gas stations in order to reduce the impact of high oil prices.
Fuel sales rose 14.7% month-on-month in October after a 17.4% drop in September.
Economists said sales were likely to rise further in November and December, the busiest shopping months of the year because of Christmas.

"This still shouldn't worry the (National Bank of Poland's) Monetary Policy Council, as demand in the economy is not currently hot enough to stimulate inflation," said Monika Kurtek, chief economist at Bank Pocztowy.
Kurtek said the central bank could leave interest rates unchanged in December, as it did in November.
